n: The Lord sends Sidney Rigdon, Parley P. Pratt, and Leman Copley to preach to the Shakers near Cleveland, Ohio. They are to teach the gospel just as they received it, not watered down.

f.g: The United Society of Believers in Christ’s Second Appearing, a celibate communal group named for the shaking in their worship.
Leman Copley, a recent convert who had formerly been a Shaker.

n: The Shakers want part of the truth, but not all of it. They are not right before the Lord and need to repent.
Sidney and Parley, experienced preachers, are the main messengers.
Leman is to be ordained and reason with the Shakers, but only on the basis of what Sidney and Parley teach him—not his old Shaker beliefs. Obedience would bring blessing.

f.w: not according to that which he has received of them
f.g: Leman still held some Shaker ideas; he is told to set them aside.

n: God the Father speaks of sending his Only Begotten Son to redeem the world. Salvation depends on receiving Christ.

People treated the Son of Man as they pleased, even crucifying him; yet he now reigns in heaven and will descend to put all enemies under his feet. The Shakers believed Christ had already returned—this verse says he has not yet.

f.w: put all enemies under his feet

n: No one—not even the angels—knows the day and hour of his coming. This directly answered Shaker claims that the Second Coming had already happened.

f.w: the hour and the day no man knoweth

n: All people need repentance, for all are under sin—except holy men the Lord has reserved, unknown to the elders. Latter-day Saints often understand these to include translated beings.

f.w: holy men that ye know not of

n: The Lord has restored his everlasting covenant—the gospel that has existed from the beginning.
God fulfills his promises. The nations will bow to this covenant; those that exalt themselves will be humbled by his power.

f.w: that which is now exalted of itself shall be laid low

n: The missionaries are to preach as Peter did on the day of Pentecost.

f.w: mine apostle of old, whose name was Peter

n: First, believe in Jesus, who lived on earth and is yet to come—the beginning and the end.

f.g: Emphasizes his Second Coming is still future, contrary to Shaker belief.

n: Then repent and be baptized in Christ’s name for the forgiveness of sins—as Peter taught. The Shakers did not practice baptism.
Those who do will receive the gift of the Holy Ghost by the laying on of hands by elders.

f.w: by the laying on of the hands

n: Anyone who forbids marriage is not sent by God, because marriage is God’s institution. The Shakers required celibacy.
It is right for a man to have a wife, and the two become one flesh, so the earth may fulfill the purpose of its creation.

f.w: they twain shall be one flesh

n: Marriage and family allow the earth to be filled with the number of God’s spirit children planned before the world was made.

f.g: The full number of human beings God intended to send to earth.

n: Anyone who commands people to abstain from meat is not sent by God. Some Shakers avoided pork or meat.
Animals, birds, and plants are provided for human food and clothing, in abundance.

f.w: is ordained for the use of man

n: Yet no one should possess more than another—inequality is part of why the world lies in sin. This echoes the law of consecration.

f.w: not given that one man should possess that which is above another

n: Woe to anyone who kills animals or wastes meat without need. God’s gifts are not to be squandered.

f.w: wasteth flesh and hath no need

n: The Son of Man will not come as a woman, nor as a man walking about on earth. The Shakers believed Christ’s second appearing had come through their founder, Ann Lee.

f.g: A direct correction of the Shaker teaching about Ann Lee.

f.w: neither of a man traveling on the earth

n: Don’t be deceived; stay steady and watch for his true coming, when heaven shakes, the earth reels like a drunkard, valleys rise, and mountains fall—all at the angel’s trumpet.

f.w: reel to and fro as a drunken man
for the valleys to be exalted

n: Before that great day, Jacob (Israel) will flourish in the wilderness and the Lamanites will blossom like a rose.

f.w: the Lamanites shall blossom as the rose

n: Zion will flourish on the hills and mountains and be gathered to the place the Lord has appointed.

f.w: Zion shall flourish upon the hills

n: The missionaries are to go, repent of their own sins, and ask and knock in prayer.

f.w: ask and ye shall receive; knock and it shall be opened unto you

n: The Lord will go ahead of them and guard them from behind, and be among them. They will not be confused or defeated.

f.g: Put to shame or thrown into confusion.

n: Jesus Christ signs the revelation, declaring that he comes quickly. (The Shakers largely rejected the elders’ message.)
